reply_text:
Let me find the 大象 notebook and read what it actually uses from Fong and the related causal theories before revising.The notebook's own text and the Dark Tower v3 report give me what the letter left out. Adding a paragraph on the open causal theories and committing.㊥ (gist) The letter now has a paragraph on the open causal theories, in the file at the same path. But first something you should know: the draft on disk is not mine any more. claude-19 rewrote it at 03:07Z, apparently from the same prompt, into a shorter and more cautious letter with a claim ledger that deliberately left out the categorical material. Your concern applies to that version even more than to mine, and I added the paragraph to it.

㊩ (what went wrong on my side) My edit script checked for my own text, failed to find it, and stopped. The following `git add` was not chained to that check, so it committed claude-19's rewrite under my commit message (30cd02d4f). The record is corrected in the next commit's message rather than by amending, per the shared-tree rule.

㊢ ("Fong/related causal theories used in the daxiang notebook") The new paragraph (2bc17b9cb) says, in the rewritten letter's register: a pattern's DAG presents a causal theory in the sense of Fong's 2012 thesis, the free copy-discard category on its variables and mechanisms, and the Boolean equations are an open model of it in Set after Lorenz and Tull; an incident is the gluing of the patterns that bear on it; gluing identifies by shared name and refuses on an undeclared share, a doubly owned variable, or a cycle. It includes the Dark Tower v3 correction: this is not decorated-cospan composition but gluing in the cospan operad restricted to copy-discard diagrams, and the two refusals are Fritz and Liang's left-monogamy and acyclicity. It names what was computed on the red-tape incident (cone, counterfactual, 103 untested independencies) and the two wanted extensions, Markov-category mechanisms and promises as processes with a hole. Three ledger entries cite the notebook's references, the v3 report, and the mission's skeleton section.

㊟ (two drafts) The letter you now have is claude-19's frame plus this paragraph. My longer version (the Dark Tower questions to him, the 238 Lean files, the dialogue-lab totals) is in git at 420745f8c if you want any of it back. Which frame you prefer is yours to pick; I would not send both seats the same prompt again without one of us knowing.

previous_reply_acts.text: (what it says) It meets the project at its four parts in turn. DiagramProver: the 489-problem curriculum corpus, the April run's numbers, tactic traces as string diagrams with goal-state types as ports. Formal requirements first: the 238 War Machine Lean files as the specification the code conforms to. Where diagrams meet our mathematics: the Dark Tower notes already build on Simmons and Kissinger's Caus[𝒞] and BV paper, and the June grounding pass left three underdetermined items that were written down as "questions to carry to Kissinger" and never sent, so the letter asks them. The futon6 dependency graph with its review buffer as a corpus-and-review loop for the graphical algebraic geometry case study. And the co-creation assessment, where the labelled dialogue grammar and author-not-reviewer reviewing are what we have to offer.

previous_reply_acts.text: (things to check before sending) The three conjecture questions are taken from the 2026-06-12 checkpoint in the second Dark Tower note; you may want to reread that section and decide whether they are the questions you would ask him today. The proof-landscape numbers are from April and say so. I left out mfuton, since the shared repository is Rob's and the Lean parser work is his to describe, and I named no collaborators.
